schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `digits` (`d` TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `seq_1m` (`n` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `dim_customer` (`customer_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, `region` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, `customer_tier` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `dim_product` (`product_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, `category` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, `active` TINYINT(1) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fact_order` (`order_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, `customer_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, `status` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, `order_date` DATE NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fact_order_item` (`order_item_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, `order_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, `product_id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, `quantity` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, `unit_price` DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL)
generation_sql: INSERT IGNORE INTO `seq_1m` (`n`) SELECT 1 + d1.d + 10 * d2.d + 100 * d3.d + 1000 * d4.d + 10000 * d5.d + 100000 * d6.d FROM `digits` d1 CROSS JOIN `digits` d2 CROSS JOIN `digits` d3 CROSS JOIN `digits` d4 CROSS JOIN `digits` d5 CROSS JOIN `digits` d6 WHERE 1 + d1.d + 10 * d2.d + 100 * d3.d + 1000 * d4.d + 10000 * d5.d + 100000 * d6.d <= 1000000

INSERT IGNORE INTO `dim_customer` (`customer_id`, `region`, `customer_tier`) SELECT n, CASE WHEN MOD(n, 100) < 70 THEN 'NA' WHEN MOD(n, 100) < 90 THEN 'EU' WHEN MOD(n, 100) < 99 THEN 'APAC' ELSE 'LATAM' END, CASE WHEN MOD(n, 10) < 8 THEN 'standard' ELSE 'vip' END FROM `seq_1m` WHERE n <= 50000

INSERT IGNORE INTO `dim_product` (`product_id`, `category`, `active`) SELECT n, CASE WHEN MOD(n, 100) = 0 THEN 'featured' WHEN MOD(n, 20) = 0 THEN 'seasonal' ELSE 'regular' END, CASE WHEN MOD(n, 50) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END FROM `seq_1m` WHERE n <= 5000

INSERT IGNORE INTO `fact_order` (`order_id`, `customer_id`, `status`, `order_date`) SELECT n, 1 + MOD(n * 37, 50000), CASE WHEN MOD(n, 100) < 85 THEN 'COMPLETE' WHEN MOD(n, 100) < 95 THEN 'PENDING' ELSE 'CANCELLED' END, DATE_ADD('2020-01-01', INTERVAL MOD(n, 730) DAY) FROM `seq_1m` WHERE n <= 200000

INSERT IGNORE INTO `fact_order_item` (`order_item_id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `quantity`, `unit_price`) SELECT ((o.n - 1) * 3) + i.item_no, o.n, CASE WHEN MOD(o.n, 100) = 0 AND i.item_no = 1 THEN 1 + MOD(o.n, 50) ELSE 1 + MOD(o.n * 13 + i.item_no * 7, 5000) END, 1 + MOD(o.n + i.item_no, 5), ROUND(100 + MOD(o.n * 17 + i.item_no * 11, 9900) / 100, 2) FROM `seq_1m` o JOIN (SELECT 1 AS item_no UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) i WHERE o.n <= 200000

tables.name: digits
tables.purpose: Small helper table for bounded number generation
tables.distribution_notes: Uniform digits 0-9; used only to build a synthetic sequence table.

tables.name: seq_1m
tables.purpose: Bounded helper sequence table used to generate deterministic synthetic rows
tables.distribution_notes: Dense contiguous integers provide stable bulk-load generation and reproducible cardinalities.

tables.name: dim_customer
tables.purpose: Customer dimension used in selective joins and region filtering
tables.distribution_notes: Region is skewed toward NA to create a common filter with moderate selectivity; customer tier is secondary skew.

tables.name: dim_product
tables.purpose: Product dimension used in selective joins and category filtering
tables.distribution_notes: Category is highly skewed, with featured products rare so the filter stays selective and amplifies join work.

tables.name: fact_order
tables.purpose: Order fact table providing the main filtered join driver
tables.distribution_notes: Status is skewed heavily toward COMPLETE to keep many rows participating; customer_id spreads across the customer dimension.

tables.name: fact_order_item
tables.purpose: High-fanout line-item fact table that drives repeated join work
tables.distribution_notes: Three items per order on average; join to order_id has no supporting index beyond the primary key on order_item_id.

value_skew.fact_order_item.product_id: mostly spread across regular products with a rare featured-product overlap

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.region, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM `fact_order` o JOIN `dim_customer` c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN `fact_order_item` oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN `dim_product` p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'COMPLETE' AND c.region = 'NA' AND p.category = 'featured' GROUP BY o.order_id, c.region ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 20
calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the synthetic data produces a join-heavy plan with selective filters and enough fanout to make CPU the dominant resource.
expected_evidence: The plan includes all four tables and preserves the multi-stage join structure from the incident description.
The predicates on status, region, and category materially affect the estimated row counts.
The large fact table dominates the work because the line-item join lacks a direct supporting index on order_id.
